newsitem.title: USA: European rapeseed said sold to Canada - trade.
newsitem.headline: European rapeseed said sold to Canada - trade.

text.p: Indications are that 15,000 to 40,000 tonnes of European rapeseed was sold earlier this week to a Canadian crusher in what appeared to be a sign that Canadian canola prices were too high, Canadian sources said.
"The talk around here was that it was a political ploy to try to talk the Canadian canola market down," said a Canadian analyst in Winnipeg who declined to be identified.
He said he believed at least 15,000 to 30,000 tonnes of rapeseed from Europe was traded for July shipment, probably through the port of Rotterdam.
Canada is top producer of canola, a rapeseed hybrid.
Several sources said the European business was likely done early this week but the move was not a big surprise.

"This has happened in the past, where the threat has been made to bring in rapeseed from the European Union to Canada," the analyst said. "This is more of a signal to the Canadian canola farmer that the price is too high," he said.
A second Canadian analyst said he understood two cargoes totalling nearly 40,000 tonnes of rapeseed were sold to Canada.
"It was probably 36,000 to 38,000 tonnes. We think it was French (origin) and we understand it was for July/August shipment," he said.

He said European rapeseed prices were about US$30 per tonne under Canadian prices. The two cargoes were probably destined for Windsor, Ontario, with the cost about US$300 per tonne, C and F, the second analyst said.
A third trade source said at least one to two cargoes up up to 40,000 tonnes total of European rapeseed was sold to a Canadian crusher in Ontario for July/August shipment.
European rapeseed values have become very competitive, particularly new crop.
"The (European) seed was cheaper," he said. "If Canadian canola prices stay where they are, then more European rapeseed could be coming to Canada." ((Doris Frankel 312-983-7305))
